subproblem.title: Passage to the limit in a Sobolev bound along C¹ approximations with uniformly bounded, a.e. convergent derivatives supported in a fixed compact set
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : ℝ≥0∞) (c : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0) (S : Set (Rn N)) (u : Rn N → ℝ) (v : ℕ → Rn N → ℝ), IsCompact S → (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (v j)) → (∀ j, tsupport (v j) ⊆ S) → (∀ j y, ‖fderiv ℝ (v j) y‖ ≤ K) → (∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure (Rn N)), Tendsto (fun j ↦ v j y) atTop (𝓝 (u y))) → (∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure (Rn N)), Tendsto (fun j ↦ fderiv ℝ (v j) y) atTop (𝓝 (fderiv ℝ u y))) → (∀ j, eLpNorm (v j) p volume ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * ∫ y, ‖fderiv ℝ (v j) y‖)) → eLpNorm u p volume ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * ∫ y, ‖fderiv ℝ u y‖)
subproblem.natural_proof:
(Implementation notes: every lemma named below is already in the import closure of GMT.Ch03.Submission.
- Fatou's inequality for eLpNorm is MeasureTheory.Lp.eLpNorm_lim_le_liminf_eLpNorm (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.LpSpace.Complete). It lives in namespace MeasureTheory.Lp, so write Lp.eLpNorm_lim_le_liminf_eLpNorm. It holds for every exponent p, and in this Mathlib it also takes AEStronglyMeasurable of the limit function.
- Dominated convergence is tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DominatedConvergence).
- An a.e. limit of a.e. strongly measurable functions is a.e. strongly measurable by aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae.)
Source: parent proof Steps 4 and 5: convergence of the gradient integrals by dominated convergence, and Fatou's lemma for eLpNorm. Here the approximating sequence and its properties are taken as hypotheses. Notation: L^N := volume on Rn N; Dw(y) := fderiv ℝ w y, with operator norm ‖Dw(y)‖.

Assume:
- S is compact;
- each v_j is C¹ with tsupport v_j ⊆ S;
- ‖Dv_j(y)‖ ≤ K for all j and y;
- v_j → u L^N-a.e.;
- Dv_j → Du L^N-a.e.;
- eLpNorm v_j p L^N ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c ∫ ‖Dv_j‖ dL^N) for every j.
1. (Measurability.) Each v_j is continuous (being C¹), hence a.e. strongly measurable. Since v_j(y) → u(y) for L^N-a.e. y, u is a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae along atTop).
2. (Domination.) Let g := S.indicator (fun _ ↦ K), so g(y) = K for y ∈ S and g(y) = 0 otherwise. Then ‖Dv_j(y)‖ ≤ g(y) for all j and y. If y ∈ S this is the hypothesis. If y ∉ S, then y ∉ tsupport v_j, so v_j vanishes on a neighbourhood of y and Dv_j(y) = 0 (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport). g is integrable: S is compact, hence closed (so measurable) and of finite measure (IsCompact.measure_lt_top), so the constant K is integrable on S and its indicator is integrable (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator).
3. (Pointwise data.) Each y ↦ ‖Dv_j(y)‖ is continuous, because Dv_j is continuous when v_j is C¹; hence it is a.e. strongly measurable. For L^N-a.e. y, Dv_j(y) → Du(y) in Rn N →L[ℝ] ℝ, so ‖Dv_j(y)‖ → ‖Du(y)‖ by continuity of the norm.
4. (Gradient integrals converge.) Dominated convergence with steps 2 and 3 gives ∫ ‖Dv_j‖ dL^N → ∫ ‖Du‖ dL^N. By continuity of t ↦ c·t and of ENNReal.ofReal, a_j := ENNReal.ofReal(c ∫ ‖Dv_j‖) → a := ENNReal.ofReal(c ∫ ‖Du‖) in ℝ≥0∞. Therefore liminf_j a_j = a.
5. (Fatou.) By step 1 and the a.e. convergence v_j → u, eLpNorm u p L^N ≤ liminf_j eLpNorm v_j p L^N (Lp.eLpNorm_lim_le_liminf_eLpNorm). This holds for every p ∈ [0, ∞], including p = ∞.
6. (Comparison.) eLpNorm v_j p L^N ≤ a_j for every j, so monotonicity of liminf in the complete lattice ℝ≥0∞ gives liminf_j eLpNorm v_j p L^N ≤ liminf_j a_j = a.
7. Combining steps 5 and 6: eLpNorm u p L^N ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c ∫ ‖Du‖ dL^N). ∎
proof_key_steps: Each v_j is continuous, hence a.e. strongly measurable; u is a.e. strongly measurable as their a.e. limit.
‖fderiv ℝ (v j)‖ ≤ S.indicator (fun _ ↦ K), because fderiv vanishes off tsupport (v j) ⊆ S, and this bound is integrable since S is compact.
Dominated convergence gives ∫‖fderiv ℝ (v j)‖ → ∫‖fderiv ℝ u‖, so ofReal(c∫‖fderiv ℝ (v j)‖) → ofReal(c∫‖fderiv ℝ u‖), which is then the liminf.
Lp.eLpNorm_lim_le_liminf_eLpNorm: eLpNorm u p ≤ liminf eLpNorm (v j) p ≤ liminf ofReal(c∫‖fderiv ℝ (v j)‖) = ofReal(c∫‖fderiv ℝ u‖).

audit.reason: All hypotheses match the Lean proposition. The compact set supplies an integrable indicator bound; derivative convergence gives dominated convergence, and value convergence supplies measurability of u. Fatou and continuity of ENNReal.ofReal(c·) prove the exact conclusion, including p = 0, p = ∞ and arbitrary real c. No hidden regularity assumption or circular reliance is needed; the bare identifier is unreserved.
